newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle trade quiet,no sales-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle trade quiet,no sales-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains cattle feedlots early Friday were quiet following this week's active sales, feedlot sources said.
Sales this week occured at $69.00 per cwt, up $1.00 from last week, with the bulk of cattle trading on Tuesday, although there was moderate trade on Thursday, they said.
Several loads of cattle sold on Tuesday were picked up early Friday, as packers continued to meet active beef demand, sources said.
Beef demand was fueled by seasonal retail demand for Memorial Day holiday beef features, they said.
Fed cattle next week were seen priced at $70.00 per cwt, with support seen from projections for smaller showlists than this week's, a cattle feeder said.
However, lower beef prices on Wednesday and Thursday suggested the market had topped and that beef demand was tapering, market sources said.
Beef prices on Thursday were down $0.24 to $0.69 per cwt, with 240 fabricated beef loads sold. Heavyweight choice beef was quoted down $0.44 at $107.07, a $1.51 drop in two days, USDA reported.
